description:
The food.gdt dataset is open in Gretl. It contains real household survey data with two variables: 'food_exp' (weekly food expenditure in dollars) and 'income' (weekly income in $100 units) for 40 households.

Run an OLS (Ordinary Least Squares) regression with 'food_exp' as the dependent variable and 'income' as the independent variable. Use the menu: Model > Ordinary Least Squares. In the dialog, set food_exp as the dependent variable and income as the regressor, then click OK. After the results window appears, save the model output as a text file to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/ols_results.txt using File > Save to file (or the save icon) in the results window.

metadata.data_source: Hill, Griffiths, Lim - Principles of Econometrics 5th ed, household survey data
